info.title: SpiritStream HTTP API
info.description: Versioned REST surface for SpiritStream. All clients (web, Tauri desktop, Tauri mobile, CLI, automation) speak this API. See the rewrite plan for the migration shape.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/audit/log` — paginated, filterable read of the audit
get.description:
log. Entries are serialised as-is from
[`spiritstream_core::services::AuditEntry`]. The response is wrapped
in an HMAC-verification status (`tampered: bool` + last
known-good sequence) so the UI can render the red banner.

400.description: Validation: chat not configured / retry unsupported / no active stream.
Empty message or no platforms enabled.

200.description: Tokens + user info persisted to active profile.

401.description: OAuth provider rejected the code or returned no user data.

409.description: No active profile to bind tokens to.
No active profile to bind tokens to.

get.summary: `GET /profiles/locked` — list every encrypted profile currently unlocked
get.description: in the session. The frontend uses this to render lock/unlock icons.

404.description: One of the submitted profile names doesn't exist.

get.summary: `GET /profiles/{name}` — return the full profile body. `password` is
get.description:
required as a query parameter for encrypted profiles; plaintext profiles
ignore it. Encrypted-but-no-password returns 401 `password_required`.

put.summary: `PUT /profiles/{name}` — create or update a profile. The request body
put.description:
contains the full profile + optional encryption password.

Server-side validation enforced (see `ProfileManager::save_with_key_encryption`):
- profile name charset/length
- RTMP input port-conflict with other profiles
- URL normalization via `PlatformRegistry::normalize_url`

post.summary: `POST /profiles/{name}/activate` — load the profile, set it as the active
post.description:
session profile, propagate to chat/OBS handlers, emit the consolidated
`profile_activated` event. The frontend used to do this cascade in
`profileStore.applyProfileSettings`; now it just listens for the event.

409.description: Activation precondition not met (e.g. no active profile resolvable).

post.description:
Replaces the frontend's two-round-trip flow in
`apps/web/src/stores/profileStore.ts` (load with password → save without
password). The server loads the profile with the supplied password and
re-saves it WITHOUT encryption in one operation.

On success the profile also gets added to the session unlock set so
subsequent reads don't re-prompt for a password before the profile list
refreshes.

get.summary: `GET /profiles/{name}/encrypted` — quick check whether a profile is stored encrypted on disk.

post.summary: `POST /profiles/{name}/lock` — remove the profile from the session unlock
post.description: set. After this call, accessing the profile again requires the password.

post.summary: `POST /profiles/{name}/unlock` — validate the password and add the
post.description:
profile to the server-side session unlock set, replacing
`Profiles.tsx`'s frontend `unlockedProfiles: Set<string>` state.

503.description: One or more critical subsystems failed their check.

post.description:
Coordinates: stop every active stream, disconnect every chat
platform, disconnect OBS, wipe in-memory secret caches, record an
audit-log entry, emit `panic_triggered`. See
[`spiritstream_core::services::SafetyService`] for the contract.

**No confirmation token is required** — that defeats the purpose of
a panic button. The rate limiter applies (`default_auth`) so a
malicious script can't burn the panic call to mask real intent.

get.summary: `GET /settings` — return the resolved (cached) global settings document.

put.summary: `PUT /settings` — replace the global settings document. Field-level bound
put.description:
checks (`log_retention_days` ∈ [1, 365], `discord_cooldown_seconds`
∈ [0, 86400], `backend_port` ∈ [1, 65535]) run inside
`SettingsManager::save`. Out-of-range values return 400
`validation_failed` with the full list of offending fields.

delete.summary: `DELETE /settings/data` — wipe every persisted setting + every profile.
delete.description:
A per-call confirmation token will gate this in the future; for now the
authenticated session is the only gate.

post.description:
`<export_path>/`. The destination must resolve inside the app data dir or
the user's home; anything else returns 403 `path_outside_allowed_root`.

get.summary: `GET /settings/profiles-path` — return the absolute on-disk path of the
get.description:
profiles directory for the active install. The frontend uses it for the
"open profiles folder" affordance.

get.summary: `GET /streams` — snapshot of which output groups are currently streaming.
get.description:
The full real-time stats path stays on the WebSocket; this endpoint is
the typed REST shape callers reach for when they only need "is anything
running right now."

post.summary: `POST /streams` — start every output group with at least one enabled
post.description: target. Same chat-side-effect orchestration as the single-group form.

422.description: FFmpeg binary missing or encoder unavailable.

delete.summary: `DELETE /streams` — stop every group and disconnect chat.

post.summary: `POST /streams/groups/{group_id}` — start streaming for a single output
post.description:
group. The transport layer wires the chat auto-connect side effects via
the same helpers the legacy invoke path used (`auto_connect_chat_platforms`,
`start_log_session`) until the ChatService boundary fully tightens.

422.description: FFmpeg binary missing or encoder unavailable.

delete.description: chat auto-disconnect when no groups remain.

400.description: Validation: group not in active set / already streaming / retries exhausted.

patch.description:
state and restart its parent group with the updated filter. PATCH (not
PUT) because the body is a partial update — `enabled` flag plus the
group context needed to restart, not a full replacement of the target.

post.description:
at the plan's "Validation strategy" note: server is authoritative; the
frontend may call this for live feedback in modals, but the same check
runs inside `POST /streams`.

Returns 200 with `{valid: true}` on success, 400
`invalid_stream_config` with `reasons: Vec<ValidationIssue>` on failure.

get.description: Returned once on app start, cached by the frontend.

`OutputGroupModal.tsx:22-111` constants. Returned once on app start,
cached by the frontend.

400.description: Theme file invalid (bad JSON, missing required tokens, etc.).

500.description: Internal error reading or copying the file.

message.description: Optional human-readable message. Internal details are never included.

chain.description:
HMAC chain status. The audit-log UI inspects this on
every fetch; a `tampered` value triggers the red banner.
Always computed server-side against the on-disk log; clients cannot influence it.

entries.description: Page slice (oldest-first within the returned window).

total.description: Total entries that survive the filter (before paging).

chatMaxChars.description:
Per-platform chat message max length (already exposed via
`ChatPlatform::max_message_chars`, mirrored here for convenience).

chatOverlayPollMs.description: Polling interval for chat overlay state (ms).

chatPollIntervalMs.description: Polling interval for refreshing chat platform status (ms).

obsTriggerDelayMs.description: Delay before triggering SpiritStream when OBS starts streaming (ms).

retryBaseDelayMs.description: Base delay for HTTP retry with exponential back-off (ms).

themeInitTimeoutMs.description:
Hard timeout for theme initialization on app start (ms). After this,
the UI falls back to the default theme rather than blocking forever.

themeTokenRetryDelayMs.description: Delay between theme-token fetch retry attempts (ms).

presets.description:
Map of encoder kind → preset list. Keys: `libx264`, `libx265`,
`nvenc`, `amf`. Frontend maps the user's selected codec to the
matching list.

services.description:
Per-subsystem report. Frontend status views render
each entry as its own row with the corresponding badge.

status.description:
Aggregate status string — `"ok"`, `"degraded"`, or `"tampered"`.
Kept for backwards-compat with Tauri sidecar polling + the
Docker `HEALTHCHECK` directive, which just need 200 + a key
they can grep for.

password.description: Password for encrypted profiles. Plaintext profiles ignore this field.
Password protecting the on-disk encrypted profile.

decrypted.description: `true` once the profile is re-saved unencrypted on disk.

unlocked.description: Names of currently-unlocked encrypted profiles for this session.

password.description: Optional password — when present the profile is encrypted on disk.

profile.description: Full profile body (matches the `Profile` ts-rs export).

password.description: Password for encrypted profiles. Plaintext profiles ignore this field.
Required password — decryption fails on mismatch with 401.

unlocked.description: Whether this profile is now in the session's unlocked set.

error.description: Short human-readable error from the subsystem.

errors.description: Per-subsystem failure detail. Empty when `ready` is true.

failed.description: Names of subsystems that failed their check. Empty when `ready` is true.

ready.description: `true` when every critical subsystem reports healthy.

elapsedMs.description: Wall-clock duration of the panic flow, in milliseconds.

streamsStopped.description: Number of active streams that were stopped by the panic.

exportPath.description:
Absolute path of the destination directory. Must resolve inside the
app data dir or the user's home — anything else is rejected with
`path_outside_allowed_root`.

settings.description: Full settings body (matches the `Settings` ts-rs export).

activeGroupIds.description: Group IDs of every output group with at least one active FFmpeg process.

profile.description:
Full profile body (matches the `Profile` ts-rs export). Encoding-config
rules (bitrate / keyframe / resolution / fps) are evaluated server-side.

valid.description:
`true` when every output group passes bound checks. `false` when one
or more `ValidationIssue`s would be returned by `POST /streams`.

oneOf.description:
Functioning but in a degraded state. `detail` carries the
reason (e.g. `"FFmpeg not on PATH; using bundled binary"`).
Subsystem requires user attention. `detail` describes why.

Audit-log tamper detection found a chain break. The number is
the last verified sequence so the UI can render the red banner.

SubsystemStatus.description:
Per-subsystem status report.

Each variant maps cleanly to a UI badge color: `ok` → green,
`degraded` → amber, `disconnected`/`tampered` → red. Adding a new
variant is a deliberate act — every subsystem reports through this
enum so the surface stays bounded.
